record.paper_title: Variants of the focusing NLS equation. Derivation, justification and open problems related to filamentation
record.original_question:
When partial off-axis variation of the group velocity and longitudinal self-steepening are both present in the same direction, namely for

 i(1 - epsilon^2 partial_z^2) partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + i epsilon partial_z)(|v|^2 v) = 0,

do solutions still exhibit self-steepening, or does the off-axis regularization suppress or qualitatively change that shock-like steepening effect?

evidence.quote: Then, one may wonder whether the partial off-axis variation of the group velocity prevents the self-steepening from taking place.
Open Problem 8. Do the solutions to equation (72) exhibit the phenomenon of self-steepening?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger-type equation with mixed partial off-axis dispersion and longitudinal self-steepening, posed for a complex-valued function v = v(t, z, x_⊥), where t ∈ ℝ is time, z ∈ ℝ is the longitudinal spatial variable, x_⊥ ∈ ℝ^{d-1} are the transverse spatial variables, Δ = ∂_z^2 + Δ_{x_⊥} is the full spatial Laplacian, and ε > 0 is a small parameter:

  i(1 − ε² ∂_z²) ∂_t v + Δ v + (1 + i ε ∂_z)(|v|² v) = 0.

The classical focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation (the case ε = 0 with a self-steepening derivative correction) is known to develop the phenomenon of "self-steepening", in which the amplitude profile of the wave forms a steepening front in the longitudinal direction z, leading to shock-like gradient blow-up of |v| or its derivatives along z. The operator (1 − ε² ∂_z²) on the time derivative encodes a partial off-axis variation of the group velocity that is known, in related models, to regularize or prevent certain singular behaviors.

Question: For sufficiently regular initial data, do solutions of the equation above still exhibit the self-steepening phenomenon (i.e., longitudinal shock-like steepening of |v|), or does the partial off-axis regularization provided by the operator (1 − ε² ∂_z²) suppress or qualitatively alter this steepening effect? Provide either a proof that self-steepening (in a precise sense, e.g., blow-up of ‖∂_z v‖_{L^∞} in finite time for some smooth, suitably localized initial data) does occur, or a proof that it is precluded by global-in-time bounds on the relevant longitudinal derivatives.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any work resolving whether solutions of this specific mixed off-axis / self-steepening NLS variant develop self-steepening, nor any proof that the off-axis term suppresses it. The problem appears to remain open, with related literature only addressing self-steepening in standard or PT-symmetric modified NLS settings, not this off-axis-regularized model.

status_evidence.title: Stabilization of self-steepening optical solitons in a periodic PT-symmetric potential
status_evidence.snippet: Studies self-steepening solitons of a modified NLS equation and their stabilization by PT-symmetric potentials, but does not treat the off-axis variant (1 − ε² ∂_z²) ∂_t v + Δ v + (1 + i ε ∂_z)(|v|² v) = 0.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the off-axis self-steepening question is provided in this related work.

status_evidence.title: Self-steepening — Prefetch
status_evidence.snippet: General description of self-steepening as shock-like distortion of pulses in nonlinear media; no analysis of the off-axis regularized model.
status_evidence.claim: Background on self-steepening but no answer to the off-axis question.
